intro.headline: Every detail represents a standard.
intro.body: A uniform is the first thing anyone in your building reads about the people working in it. Shirt colour identifies the service line, the chest logo identifies the company, and the name badge and photo ID identify the person — so nobody in your facility ever has to wonder who is on their floor or why.

photo.alt: Apex facility supervisor in uniform walking a client office floor with a checklist

spec.title: Service-line colour
spec.detail: Shirt colour says which team a person belongs to before anyone reads a badge — blue for housekeeping, green for landscaping, navy for technical, black for security, white for pantry and grey for supervision.
spec.alt: Apex teams in service-line uniform colours

spec.title: Chest logo
spec.detail: Wearer's left chest, 70 mm wide, embroidered flat stitch. The same mark on every shirt, every site, every service line.
spec.alt: Close crop of the embroidered Apex chest logo

spec.title: Name badge
spec.detail: Wearer's right chest, 75 x 24 mm. Name over role, so the person in front of you can be addressed by name rather than flagged down.
spec.alt: Close crop of the Apex name badge

spec.title: Photo ID
spec.detail: 86 x 54 mm card on a breakaway lanyard. Photo, name, staff ID, site, and a colour band matching the service line.
spec.alt: Close crop of an Apex photo ID card on a lanyard

spec.title: Supervisor grade
spec.detail: Supervisors carry a shoulder marking, so the person accountable on site is identifiable at a glance rather than by asking around.

spec.title: Service tape
spec.detail: Left sleeve, service line printed in full — housekeeping, security, technical, landscape, pest or pantry.

spec.title: Reflective hem
spec.detail: Technical and night-shift grades carry a 20 mm reflective band, because plant rooms and basements are not lit like offices.
spec.alt: Apex technician working in a plant room
